title: Henri Pigozzi, Fiat and the birth of Simca in France
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: Simca did not begin from a blank page. The marque was built around Henri Pigozzi to manufacture in France Fiat cars that had become too expensive to import.
content:
To understand Simca, one has to begin with Henri Theodore Pigozzi. The marque does not start with a heroic car, but with a very concrete industrial question: how to keep selling Fiats when customs duties make imports too expensive.

An industrial answer before a style adventure

Pigozzi knows Fiat, its products and its sales networks. His idea is to move into France part of what can no longer be sold so easily from Italy. It is a matter of manufacturing and local implantation, not only of rebadging.

That origin explains much of the Simca tone. The marque grows quickly because it is first built as a viable solution, supported by a clear industrial and commercial method.

From SAFAF to the Simca marque

Before the name Simca, there is already work in distributing and adapting Fiats to the French market. When the marque is officially created in 1934, it therefore inherits prepared ground, customer habits and a very readable direction.

The purchase of the Nanterre factory strengthens that shift. Simca is no longer only a commercial intermediary. It becomes an established manufacturer with tools and production rhythm of its own.

Why Pigozzi remains central to the story

Henri Pigozzi does not stand only as founder. He represents the early Simca way: observe the market, adapt quickly and give the popular car a strong production frame.

Even once the marque later finds its own path with the Aronde, that origin remains visible. Simca moves forward through pragmatism as much as ambition.
